title: Behavioral delta detector and soft-fallback layer for polyglot rollouts
creator: Asha Patel
description: Problem: We currently gate canary and shadow rollouts primarily on coarse token-level metrics (latency, error rate) and a handful of aggregate eval scorecards. This misses subtle behavioral regressions that only appear in certain prompt slices or on non-English inputs when rolling out new model families or quantized variants. Goal: Build a behavioral-delta detection pipeline plus a soft-fallback policy that automatically reduces weight or redirects traffic when signal-driven, cohort-aware regressions are detected. The system must support polyglot rollouts (different model families and quantization levels), per-customer golden-slices, and calibrated confidence intervals to avoid flip-flopping on low-volume noise.
acceptance_criteria:
1) A detection service ingests streaming eval probe results (golden prompt responses) and shadowed production samples and produces per-slice delta signals with bootstrapped confidence intervals.
2) The detection outputs are consumed by a soft-fallback controller that can: reduce canary weight, shift traffic to a fallback variant, or open a human review ticket.
3) Per-customer profiles and thresholds can be configured; default behavior available for unprofiled customers.
4) Integration tests validate behavior on synthetic regressions and non-regressions; dashboards show signal, CI, and actions taken.
5) End-to-end latency for detection -> action is under 2 minutes for high-priority slices.
notes: Design must avoid overfitting to noisy probes; prefer conservative thresholds with hysteresis. Use reservoir sampling for long-tail prompt coverage and ensure encryption of any customer-sensitive probes. The controller should expose a dry-run mode and a human-approval escalation path for high-risk customers.
technical_decisions: 1) Signal algorithm: use stratified bootstrap of response-level metrics (ROUGE-like similarity for structured outputs + embedding cosine divergence) instead of a single aggregated score. 2) Slicing: primary dimensions = prompt fingerprint, language, customer-tier, sequence-length-bucket. 3) CI logic: bootstrap 1k resamples to estimate delta distribution; require delta > X and p < 0.01 to trigger automatic soft-fallback. 4) Fallback action: staged weight reduction (50% -> 25% -> 0) with 10m hysteresis and an exponential backoff on re-evaluation. 5) Storage: time-series for slice signals in Cortex; artifact responses archived to S3 for audit.

risks_and_mitigations:
Risk: false positives when traffic is sparse -> Mitigation: require minimum sample counts and use per-customer adaptive thresholds.
Risk: acting too aggressively causing availability regressions -> Mitigation: soft-fallback (weighting) + human-in-loop for enterprise tiers.
Risk: compute cost of bootstrap for many slices -> Mitigation: prioritize slices by traffic and use approximate bootstrap (subsampling) for low-importance slices.
